Context/Background: UBE2M, an essential neddylation E2 enzyme, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including cancers, viral infections, and obesity. However, whether UBE2M is involved in the pathogenesis of bacterial sepsis remains unclear. In an Escherichia coli (E. coli)-induced sepsis mouse model, increased UBE2M expression in macrophages in liver and lung tissues postinfection was observed. To further clarify the role of UBE2M in macrophages, mice with macrophage-specific deletion of UBE2M were constructed.
Prompt: We isolated and purified peritoneal macrophages (PMs) from control mice and mice with UBE2M deletion.  We then stimulated PMs with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (to mimic infection) and performed RNASeq.  Based on the differential expression analysis between PMS of control (WL) vs UBE2M deletion (KL) mice under LPS stimulation, please provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways as relates to UBE2M deletion in the context of bacterial sepsis.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Macrophage-specific UBE2M deletion (KL) versus wild-type (WL) controls was profiled by RNA-Seq in peritoneal macrophages stimulated with LPS to mimic bacterial infection. Raw counts (PMC11780929-count.csv) spanned 21,884 Ensembl genes; key comparisons were KL1–3 versus WL1–3 under LPS. Definitive signals: profound up-regulation of inflammatory and cell-cycle programs in UBE2M-deficient cells, with concurrent down-regulation of mitochondrial/oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Replicate number not specified.

Across all libraries, inflammatory and cell-cycle/cytokine-signaling pathways were strongly up-enriched in UBE2M-deficient macrophages, whereas mitochondrial-metabolic and anti-inflammatory modules were suppressed. The high up/down ratio in GO processes (3.14) underscores a skew toward inflammatory and proliferative programs upon UBE2M loss. Down-enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation and ROS pathways suggests compromised mitochondrial function. Mitotic-control hallmarks (G2-M, E2F targets) and JAK-STAT signaling were among the most strongly activated, highlighting a dual effect on proliferation and immune signaling.

These filtered terms confirm robust activation of pro-inflammatory signatures (GO:0006954, Hallmark Inflammatory Response) alongside dysregulated negative-feedback modules, suggesting UBE2M deletion heightens macrophage inflammatory output.  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up-regulated:  
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function                             | Pathway(s) (examples)                                                    |  
|------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|  
| IL6  | Up        | Interleukin-6 cytokine (IL-6)             | Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction; Jak-STAT; Inflammatory Response; IL-6/JAK/STAT3 |  
| NOS2 | Up        | Nitric oxide synthase 2 (inducible)       | Chagas disease; Inflammatory Response                                    |  

Down-regulated/not observed among leading edges:  
| Gene    | Direction     | Role/Function                                   | Pathway(s)                                  |  
|---------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|  
| UBE2M   | Not observed  | Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 M (neddylation) | No leading-edge enrichments detected         |  

Comparisons  
Peritoneal macrophages mirror lung/liver findings wherein UBE2M supports inflammatory restraint and mitochondrial integrity; here, UBE2M loss shifts PMs toward hyperinflammatory and hyperproliferative states. Discordant signals (e.g., mitotic programs vs metabolic downshift) underscore complex cross-talk between cell cycle and energy metabolism.  

Implications  
UBE2M-mediated neddylation emerges as a key brake on macrophage inflammation and proliferation during sepsis. Targeting neddylation pathways may modulate macrophage activation, offering potential therapeutic angles to ameliorate sepsis-driven cytokine storms.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate NO production and IL-6 secretion in UBE2M-deficient PMs to confirm functional impact of NOS2/IL6 upregulation.  
2. Assess mitochondrial respiration (e.g., Seahorse assay) in KL versus WL PMs to corroborate down-regulated oxidative phosphorylation.  
3. Test chemical neddylation inhibitors in WT PMs to phenocopy UBE2M deletion effects on inflammatory and cell-cycle pathways.  
4. Examine expression of key negative-feedback regulators (e.g., IL10, PPARG) at protein level to gauge compensatory responses.
